Home.heroSubA: Making YOLO accessible again, the way its creators always intended it to be.
Home.heroSubB: A modern, MIT-licensed engine for training and deploying state-of-the-art object detection.
Home.communityFootnote: LibreYOLO is a huge effort. Messages like these keep us going.
Home.featuresSubtitle: Train, validate, export, and deploy detection models from one permissive, MIT-licensed package.
Home.feature1Desc: No AGPL anywhere in the dependency chain. Use it in closed-source products, SaaS, embedded systems.
Home.feature2Desc: YOLOX, YOLOv9, and RF-DETR behind a single LibreYOLO() call. Architecture, size, and class count auto-detected from weights.
Home.feature3Desc: Any input format: paths, URLs, PIL, NumPy, OpenCV, tensors, bytes. Tiled inference for large images. Auto-download weights from HuggingFace.
Home.feature4Desc: Fine-tune on custom YOLO or COCO datasets with built-in augmentation, mixed precision, and early stopping. Resume from any checkpoint.
Home.feature5Desc: COCO-standard evaluation with mAP50, mAP50-95, precision, and recall on COCO or custom datasets. Per-class metrics and confusion matrix out of the box.
Home.feature6Desc: One-line ONNX export with embedded metadata for easy deployment.
Home.deploySubtitle: Export once, run on any hardware. From $35 boards to datacenter GPUs.
Home.comparisonSubtitle: MIT means you own your work. No surprises.

OnnxIo.pillowTitle: How to reproduce Pillow's bilinear resize
OnnxIo.pillowBody: LibreYOLO resizes with Pillow's BILINEAR filter (Image.resize). It is not OpenCV INTER_LINEAR or INTER_AREA: when shrinking, Pillow widens the filter by the shrink factor, and OpenCV's resizes change detections and move boxes by several pixels. To reproduce it without Pillow, resize one axis, round to 8 bits, then resize the other axis and round again. Per axis, let s = in_size / out_size and f = max(s, 1). Output pixel i has center c = (i + 0.5) * s and reads source pixels j from int(c - f + 0.5) to int(c + f + 0.5) - 1, clipped to the image, each with weight max(0, 1 - |j + 0.5 - c| / f), divided by the sum of the weights. Pillow works in fixed point and picks the axis order from the image shape, so float weights can differ from it by one level on a few pixels. That does not change the results in our checks.

DocsLanding.licensingParagraph: LibreYOLO's code is MIT. It does not require you to open source your application, it does not reach your model weights, and it does not change if you sell what you build. Pretrained weights are separate: each one carries the license of whoever trained it, and the docs state that per checkpoint rather than averaging it into a claim. A few are non-commercial, and those say so.
DocsLanding.footer: These docs describe LibreYOLO v{version}. Documentation for earlier releases stays available at <link>/docs/versions</link>.
